claim: IL-27 is a heterodimeric cytokine that functions to constrain T cell-mediated inflammation.
source: Interleukin 27 (IL-27) is a heterodimeric cytokine that functions to constrain T cell-mediated inflammation and plays an important role in immune homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract without supporting data in this manuscript, but is presented as established knowledge.

claim: IL-27 plays an important role in immune homeostasis.
source: Interleukin 27 (IL-27) is a heterodimeric cytokine that functions to constrain T cell-mediated inflammation and plays an important role in immune homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Binding of IL-27 to cell surface receptors IL-27Rα and gp130 results in activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinases.
source: Binding of IL-27 to cell surface receptors, IL-27Rα and gp130, results in activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinases and nuclear translocation of Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (STAT1) and STAT3 transcription factors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Binding of IL-27 to cell surface receptors IL-27Rα and gp130 results in nuclear translocation of STAT1 and STAT3 transcription factors.
source: Binding of IL-27 to cell surface receptors, IL-27Rα and gp130, results in activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinases and nuclear translocation of Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (STAT1) and STAT3 transcription factors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The authors determined the quaternary structure of IL-27 bound to receptors IL-27Rα and gp130 using cryogenic-electron microscopy.
source: We used cryogenic-electron microscopy to determine the quaternary structure of IL-27, composed of p28 and Epstein-Barr Virus-Induced 3 (Ebi3) subunits, bound to receptors, IL-27Rα and gp130.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and results of the study.

claim: IL-27 is composed of p28 and Ebi3 subunits.
source: We used cryogenic-electron microscopy to determine the quaternary structure of IL-27, composed of p28 and Epstein-Barr Virus-Induced 3 (Ebi3) subunits, bound to receptors, IL-27Rα and gp130.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IL-27 composition.

claim: The structure of the IL-27 receptor complex was determined to 3.47 Å resolution.
source: The resulting 3.47 Å resolution structure revealed a three-site assembly mechanism nucleated by the central p28 subunit of the cytokine.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the resolution achieved in the study.

claim: The IL-27 receptor complex uses a three-site assembly mechanism nucleated by the central p28 subunit.
source: The resulting 3.47 Å resolution structure revealed a three-site assembly mechanism nucleated by the central p28 subunit of the cytokine.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data obtained in the study.

claim: The overall topology and molecular details of IL-27 binding are reminiscent of IL-6.
source: The overall topology and molecular details of this binding are reminiscent of IL-6 but distinct from related heterodimeric cytokines IL-12 and IL-23.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis based on the structural data obtained.

claim: The overall topology and molecular details of IL-27 binding are distinct from IL-12 and IL-23.
source: The overall topology and molecular details of this binding are reminiscent of IL-6 but distinct from related heterodimeric cytokines IL-12 and IL-23.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis based on the structural data obtained.

claim: Heterodimeric cytokines use distinct receptor assembly mechanisms.
source: These results indicate distinct receptor assembly mechanisms used by heterodimeric cytokines with important consequences for targeted agonism and antagonism of IL-27 signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural comparison of IL-27 with other heterodimeric cytokines.

claim: The distinct receptor assembly mechanisms of heterodimeric cytokines have important consequences for targeted agonism and antagonism of IL-27 signaling.
source: These results indicate distinct receptor assembly mechanisms used by heterodimeric cytokines with important consequences for targeted agonism and antagonism of IL-27 signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: Cytokines are secreted factors that mediate cell-cell communication in the immune system.
source: Cytokines are secreted factors that mediate cell-cell communication in the immune system (Spangler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Binding of cytokines to cell surface receptors leads to activation of receptor-associated JAK proteins in most cases.
source: Binding of cytokines to cell surface receptors, in most cases, leads to activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinase (JAK) proteins, which phosphorylate each other as well as downstream Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) proteins, triggering nuclear translocation and regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about cytokine signaling.

claim: JAK proteins phosphorylate each other and downstream STAT proteins.
source: Binding of cytokines to cell surface receptors, in most cases, leads to activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinase (JAK) proteins, which phosphorylate each other as well as downstream Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) proteins, triggering nuclear translocation and regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about cytokine signaling.

claim: Phosphorylation of STAT proteins triggers nuclear translocation and regulation of gene expression.
source: Binding of cytokines to cell surface receptors, in most cases, leads to activation of receptor-associated Janus Kinase (JAK) proteins, which phosphorylate each other as well as downstream Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) proteins, triggering nuclear translocation and regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about cytokine signaling.

claim: Cytokines can be classified by their use of shared receptors which transduce signals for multiple cytokines within a family.
source: Cytokines can be classified by their use of shared receptors which transduce signals for multiple cytokines within a family.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about cytokine classification.

claim: gp130 is a shared receptor that mediates signaling of multiple cytokines including IL-6, IL-11, and IL-27.
source: Interleukin-6 signal transducer (IL-6ST), also known as glycoprotein 130 (gp130), is a shared receptor that mediates signaling of multiple cytokines including IL-6, IL-11, and IL-27.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gp130.

claim: IL-27 is a heterodimeric cytokine consisting of a four-helix bundle IL-27p28 with similarity to IL-6.
source: Unlike other gp130 family cytokines, IL-27 is a heterodimeric cytokine consisting of a four-helix bundle, IL-27p28 (p28), with similarity to IL-6, complexed with a secreted binding protein, Epstein-Barr Virus-Induced 3 (Ebi3), with homology to type I cytokine receptors (Pflanz et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: IL-27p28 is complexed with Ebi3, which has homology to type I cytokine receptors.
source: Unlike other gp130 family cytokines, IL-27 is a heterodimeric cytokine consisting of a four-helix bundle, IL-27p28 (p28), with similarity to IL-6, complexed with a secreted binding protein, Epstein-Barr Virus-Induced 3 (Ebi3), with homology to type I cytokine receptors (Pflanz et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: IL-27 signals through a receptor complex consisting of IL-27Rα and gp130.
source: IL-27 signals through a receptor complex consisting of IL-27Rα (TCCR/WSX-1) and gp130 expressed on T cells, NK cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, B cells as well as subsets of endothelial and epithelial cells (Pflanz et al., 2002; Pflanz et al., 2004; Heng et al., 2008; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IL-27 receptors are expressed on T cells, NK cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, B cells, and subsets of endothelial and epithelial cells.
source: IL-27 signals through a receptor complex consisting of IL-27Rα (TCCR/WSX-1) and gp130 expressed on T cells, NK cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, B cells as well as subsets of endothelial and epithelial cells (Pflanz et al., 2002; Pflanz et al., 2004; Heng et al., 2008; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Binding of IL-27 to its receptor subunits triggers the activation of receptor-associated JAK1 and JAK2.
source: Binding of IL-27 to its receptor subunits triggers the activation of receptor-associated JAK1 and JAK2 leading to phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3 (Lucas et al., 2003; Owaki et al., 2008; Wilmes et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Activation of JAK1 and JAK2 leads to phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3.
source: Binding of IL-27 to its receptor subunits triggers the activation of receptor-associated JAK1 and JAK2 leading to phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3 (Lucas et al., 2003; Owaki et al., 2008; Wilmes et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IL-27 signaling serves to constrain inflammation by antagonizing differentiation of pro-inflammatory Th17 cells.
source: Functionally, IL-27 signaling serves to constrain inflammation by antagonizing differentiation of pro-inflammatory Th17 cells (Stumhofer et al., 2006), stimulating T-bet expression in regulatory T cells (Tregs) (Hall et al., 2012), and inducing production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 (Stumhofer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: IL-27 signaling stimulates T-bet expression in regulatory T cells.
source: Functionally, IL-27 signaling serves to constrain inflammation by antagonizing differentiation of pro-inflammatory Th17 cells (Stumhofer et al., 2006), stimulating T-bet expression in regulatory T cells (Tregs) (Hall et al., 2012), and inducing production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 (Stumhofer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: IL-27 signaling induces production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10.
source: Functionally, IL-27 signaling serves to constrain inflammation by antagonizing differentiation of pro-inflammatory Th17 cells (Stumhofer et al., 2006), stimulating T-bet expression in regulatory T cells (Tregs) (Hall et al., 2012), and inducing production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 (Stumhofer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The important role of IL-27 in constraining inflammation has prompted the development of antagonist antibodies.
source: The important role of IL-27 in constraining inflammation has prompted the development of antagonist antibodies, one of which is currently being developed as a cancer immunotherapy (Patnaik et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: An IL-27 antagonist antibody is currently being developed as a cancer immunotherapy.
source: The important role of IL-27 in constraining inflammation has prompted the development of antagonist antibodies, one of which is currently being developed as a cancer immunotherapy (Patnaik et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The heterodimeric composition of IL-27 is similar to IL-12 and IL-23.
source: Although IL-27 is a member of the gp130 family, its heterodimeric composition is similar to IL-12 and IL-23, which are cytokines that share a p40 subunit analogous to Ebi3.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on established knowledge.

claim: IL-12 and IL-23 share a p40 subunit analogous to Ebi3.
source: Although IL-27 is a member of the gp130 family, its heterodimeric composition is similar to IL-12 and IL-23, which are cytokines that share a p40 subunit analogous to Ebi3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23 directly engages the shared receptor IL-12Rβ1 in a manner distinct from IL-6 and related cytokines.
source: In this system, the p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23 directly engages the shared receptor IL-12Rβ1 in a manner distinct from IL-6 and related cytokines (Glassman et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The extracellular domain of IL-27Rα consists of five fibronectin type III (FNIII) domains (D1–5).
source: The extracellular domain of IL-27Rα consists of five fibronectin type III (FNIII) domains (D1–5) of which the N-terminal D1–D2 constitute a cytokine-binding homology region (CHR).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IL-27Rα structure.

claim: The N-terminal D1–D2 domains of IL-27Rα constitute a cytokine-binding homology region (CHR).
source: The extracellular domain of IL-27Rα consists of five fibronectin type III (FNIII) domains (D1–5) of which the N-terminal D1–D2 constitute a cytokine-binding homology region (CHR).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IL-27Rα structure.

claim: gp130 has a similar domain architecture to IL-27Rα but with the addition of an N-terminal immunoglobin (Ig) domain (D1).
source: gp130 has a similar domain architecture but with the addition of an N-terminal immunoglobin (Ig) domain (D1).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gp130 structure.

claim: Initial attempts at reconstituting a soluble receptor complex through mixing of IL-27, IL-27Rɑ D1–D2, and gp130 D1–D3 resulted in dissociation on size-exclusion chromatography due to the low affinity of gp130.
source: Initial attempts at reconstituting a soluble receptor complex through mixing of IL-27, IL-27Rɑ D1–D2, and gp130 D1–D3 resulted in dissociation on size-exclusion chromatography due to the low affinity of gp130.
evidence: This describes an experimental observation from the study.

claim: To stabilize the complex, p28 was fused to gp130 through a long (20 a.a.) flexible linker.
source: To stabilize the complex, we expressed p28 fused to gp130 through a long (20 a.a.) flexible linker which enabled us to purify the complete IL-27 receptor complex by size exclusion chromatography.
evidence: This describes the experimental strategy used in the study.

claim: The long linker did not constrain the binding mode, with ~110 Å of unresolved residues spanning a distance of 38 Å between termini.
source: Importantly, the long linker did not constrain the binding mode, with ~110 Å of unresolved residues spanning a distance of 38 Å between termini (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), but rather raised the effective concentration of gp130.
evidence: This is an observation from the structural data and is shown in a figure.

claim: The long linker raised the effective concentration of gp130.
source: Importantly, the long linker did not constrain the binding mode, with ~110 Å of unresolved residues spanning a distance of 38 Å between termini (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), but rather raised the effective concentration of gp130.
evidence: This is an inference about the function of the linker based on the experimental design.

claim: All domains of IL-27 and IL-27Rα, as well as D1 of gp130 had well resolved cryoEM density.
source: All domains of IL-27 and IL-27Rα, as well as D1 of gp130 had well resolved cryoEM density (Figure 1B-C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), with local resolution estimates near and exceeding 3 Å in this region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data obtained, supported by figures.

claim: Local resolution estimates near and exceed 3 Å in the region containing IL-27, IL-27Rα, and gp130 D1.
source: All domains of IL-27 and IL-27Rα, as well as D1 of gp130 had well resolved cryoEM density (Figure 1B-C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), with local resolution estimates near and exceeding 3 Å in this region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data obtained, supported by figures.

claim: The local resolution for the D2 density of gp130 is lower, yet able to be built with confidence.
source: The local resolution for the D2 density of gp130 is lower, yet able to be built with confidence, while D3 density was interpretable for domain placement (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data obtained, supported by figures.

claim: D3 density of gp130 was interpretable for domain placement.
source: The local resolution for the D2 density of gp130 is lower, yet able to be built with confidence, while D3 density was interpretable for domain placement (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data obtained, supported by figures.

claim: The IL-27 quaternary complex exhibits a molecular architecture containing 'sites 1–3', as seen in other gp130 family cytokines.
source: The IL-27 quaternary complex exhibits a molecular architecture containing 'sites 1–3', as seen in other gp130 family cytokines (Boulanger et al., 2003) and as hypothesized previously (Skiniotis et al., 2008; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data, supported by citations and a figure.

claim: IL-27 bridges IL-27Rα and gp130 to initiate downstream signaling through JAK1 and JAK2.
source: In this structure, IL-27 bridges IL-27Rα and gp130 to initiate downstream signaling through JAK1 and JAK2 (Ferrao et al., 2016; Pradhan et al., 2010).

claim: Within IL-27, the four-helical bundle of p28 packs against the hinge between Ebi3 D1 and D2 in a site 1 interaction.
source: Within IL-27, the four-helical bundle of p28 packs against the hinge between Ebi3 D1 and D2 in a site 1 interaction.

claim: IL-27Rα D1-D2 engages the helical face of p28 in an interaction stabilized by stem contact between the D2 domains of IL-27Rα and Ebi3 to form a site 2 interaction.
source: Opposite Ebi3, IL-27Rα D1-D2 engages the helical face of p28 in an interaction stabilized by stem contact between the D2 domains of IL-27Rα and Ebi3 to form a site 2 interaction.

claim: The D1 domain of gp130 binds to a conserved tryptophan at the tip of p28 to make a classical site 3 interaction.
source: On the posterior face of IL-27, the D1 domain of gp130 binds to a conserved tryptophan at the tip of p28 to make a classical site 3 interaction (Boulanger et al., 2003).

claim: The site 1 interface between p28 and Ebi3 is used to form the heterodimeric cytokine IL-27.
source: A site 1 interface between p28 and Ebi3 is used to form the heterodimeric cytokine IL-27.

claim: The site 1 interaction is mediated by alpha helices A and D, the AB loop, and the C-terminus of p28 packing against the hinge region between D1 and D2 of Ebi3.
source: In this interaction, the alpha helices A and D, the AB loop, and the C-terminus of p28 pack tightly against the hinge region between D1 and D2 of Ebi3 (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data, supported by a figure.

claim: The site 1 interaction is mediated by a variety of hydrogen bonds between p28 and the hinge region of Ebi3, particularly along alpha helices A and D of p28.
source: This interaction is mediated by a variety of hydrogen bonds between p28 and the hinge region of Ebi3, particularly along alpha helices A and D of p28.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data.

claim: At the center of the site 1 interface is p28 R219 which is coordinated by D207 and T209 in Ebi3.
source: At the center of this interface is p28 R219 which is coordinated by D207 and T209 in Ebi3.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data.

claim: A hydrophobic patch of residues on the C-terminus and AB loop of p28 (F94, W97, L223, W232) packs against residues in the Ebi3 hinge (F97, F157, I160).
source: Extending from this region, a hydrophobic patch of residues on the C-terminus and AB loop of p28 (F94, W97, L223, W232) packs against residues in the Ebi3 hinge (F97, F157, I160).

claim: The extensive and hydrophobic nature of the site 1 interface is consistent with the observation that co-expression of p28 and Ebi3 is required for efficient cytokine secretion.
source: The extensive and hydrophobic nature of this interface is consistent with the observation that co-expression of p28 and Ebi3 is required for efficient cytokine secretion (Pflanz et al., 2002).

claim: Alpha helices A and C of p28 form the bulk of the site 2a interaction.
source: Alpha helices A and C of p28 form the bulk of the site 2a interaction.

claim: The site 2a interaction is more limited in terms of hydrophobicity and buried surface area compared to the site 1 interaction (Site 1: 1,339.4 Å2, Site 2a: 810.4 Å2).
source: In contrast to the site 1 interaction which forms the holo-cytokine, the site 2a interaction is more limited both in terms of hydrophobicity and buried surface area (Site 1: 1,339.4 Å2, Site 2a: 810.4 Å2) (Krissinel and Henrick, 2007).

claim: A 13 amino acid polyglutamic acid region in p28 may form an alpha helix (polyE helix) and contact R74 and K77 in the IL-27Rɑ D1 domain.
source: One notable feature of this interface is the contribution of a 13 amino acid polyglutamic acid region in p28. This region is not well resolved in the cryoEM density, but may form an alpha helix (polyE helix) and contact R74 and K77 in the IL-27Rɑ D1 domain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural data due to poor resolution in this region.

claim: Cytokine binding is stabilized by 'stem-stem' interactions between D2 FNIII domains of IL-27Rα and Ebi3.
source: Cytokine binding is stabilized by 'stem-stem' interactions between D2 FNIII domains of IL-27Rα and Ebi3.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data.

claim: The site 2b interaction is characterized by a high degree of shape and charge complementarity with an arginine-rich patch of Ebi3 (R143, R171, R194) packing against the positively charged base of IL-27Rɑ D2 domain (D138, D142, E146).
source: This site 2b interaction is characterized by a high degree of shape and charge complementarity with an arginine-rich patch of Ebi3 (R143, R171, R194) packing against the positively charged base of IL-27Rɑ D2 domain (D138, D142, E146).

claim: The composite nature of IL-27Rɑ binding explains, in part, the inability of p28 to mediate IL-27 signaling in the absence of Ebi3.
source: The composite nature of IL-27Rɑ binding explains, in part, the inability of p28 to mediate IL-27 signaling in the absence of Ebi3 (Stumhofer et al., 2010).

claim: A classical site 3 interface is formed through the interaction of the D1 Ig domain of gp130 associating with both p28 (site 3a) and Ebi3 (site 3b).
source: On the posterior face of the cytokine, a classical site 3 interface is formed through the interaction of the D1 Ig domain of gp130 associating with both p28 (site 3a) and Ebi3 (site 3b) (Figure 2D, E).

claim: The site 3 interaction is anchored by the conserved W197 on p28 which packs tightly against the base of the D1 Ig domain of gp130.
source: Similar to IL-12 family members, IL-23 and IL-12 (Glassman et al., 2021a), and the gp130 family members IL-6 (Boulanger et al., 2003) and viral IL-6 (Chow et al., 2001), this interaction is anchored by the conserved W197 on p28 which packs tightly against the base of the D1 Ig domain of gp130 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data, supported by citations and a figure.

claim: The site 3 interaction is extended by the AB loop of p28 which contacts both gp130 and Ebi3.
source: The site 3 interaction is extended by the AB loop of p28 which contacts both gp130 and Ebi3.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural data.

claim: An interaction between the N-terminus of gp130 and helix D of the four-helix bundle is not observed in the IL-27 structure.
source: We do not observe an interaction between the N-terminus of gp130 and helix D of the four-helix bundle as observed for other site 3 interactions; however, this may be due to the use of a flexible GS linker which connects p28 to gp130.
evidence: This is an observation from the structural data with a speculative explanation.

claim: The tip of gp130 D1 packs against the top of Ebi3 D1 in a limited interface centered around Ebi3 F118.
source: The tip of gp130 D1 packs against the top of Ebi3 D1 in a limited interface centered around Ebi3 F118.

source: The heterodimeric nature of IL-27 has led some to classify it as an IL-12 family cytokine (Trinchieri et al., 2003).

claim: Comparison of the IL-27 receptor complex with that of IL-23 and IL-12 reveals striking differences.
source: However, comparison of the IL-27 receptor complex with that of IL-23 and IL-12 reveals striking differences (Figure 3A–C).

claim: In IL-27, the central p28 subunit engages all receptor components.
source: In IL-27, the central p28 subunit engages all receptor components.

claim: In IL-23 and IL-12, each subunit engages a different receptor in a modular interaction mechanism.
source: In contrast, each subunit of IL-23 and IL-12 engages a different receptor in a modular interaction mechanism (Glassman et al., 2021a).

claim: The assembly of IL-27 more closely resembles that of IL-6, in which the central four-helix bundle encodes binding sites for all receptor components.

claim: In IL-6, the four-helix bundle motif is duplicated through a C2 symmetry axis due to a dual role of gp130 at site 2 and site 3.
source: However, in the case of IL-6, this motif is duplicated through a C2 symmetry axis due to a dual role of gp130 at site 2 and site 3.

claim: The similarity between IL-27 and IL-6 is observed not only in overall architecture but also in molecular detail.
source: The similarity between IL-27 and IL-6 is observed not only in overall architecture but also in molecular detail, where IL-6, vIL-6, and IL-27 all engage gp130 using a highly convergent interface in which a tryptophan from helix D of the cytokine (W197 in p28, W185 in IL-6, W166 in vIL-6) forms an aromatic anchor that is capped by Y116 of gp130 (Figures 2F and 3D, E).

claim: IL-6, vIL-6, and IL-27 all engage gp130 using a highly convergent interface in which a tryptophan from helix D of the cytokine forms an aromatic anchor that is capped by Y116 of gp130.
source: The similarity between IL-27 and IL-6 is observed not only in overall architecture but also in molecular detail, where IL-6, vIL-6, and IL-27 all engage gp130 using a highly convergent interface in which a tryptophan from helix D of the cytokine (W197 in p28, W185 in IL-6, W166 in vIL-6) forms an aromatic anchor that is capped by Y116 of gp130 (Figures 2F and 3D, E).

source: Alignment of gp130 D1–(v)IL-6 pairs to the IL-27 structure reveals a tight correlation in gp130 binding pose with Cα RMSDs of 1.039 Å (IL-6) and 1.015 Å (vIL-6) across 149 and 124 trimmed residue pairs.

claim: The striking convergence of gp130 binding modes helps to explain the ability of p28 to antagonize IL-6 signaling.
source: This striking convergence of gp130 binding modes helps to explain the ability of p28 to antagonize IL-6 signaling (Stumhofer et al., 2010) and contextualizes its place in respect to both gp130 and IL-12 family cytokines.

claim: IL-27 extends the paradigm of shared receptor components mediating diverse signaling outputs, given that it shares the gp130 subunit with IL-6 but mediates distinct and often countervailing functional effects.
source: A key paradigm in cytokine structural biology is the use of shared receptor components that mediate diverse signaling outputs. IL-27 extends this, given that it shares the gp130 subunit with IL-6 but mediates distinct and often countervailing functional effects.

claim: IL-27 assembles a receptor complex reminiscent of IL-6 but distinct from other heterodimeric IL-12/23 class cytokines.

source: Ebi3 has been reported to complex with the p35 subunit of IL-12 to form IL-35 (Collison et al., 2007) and the p19 subunit of IL-23 to form IL-39 (Wang et al., 2016), while p28 has been proposed to interact with IL-6Rα (Garbers et al., 2013) and the p40 subunit of IL-12/23 (Wang et al., 2012).
